stories.headline: A famous actress saw herself on a sales video, selling face cream she had never heard of. It wasn't her. At 3 a.m. she went after them.
stories.what: On 18 Oct actress Wu Yue posted on Weibo in the early hours naming the account 花姐美肤日记, which had used AI face-swap and voice cloning to make her recommend a cheap skincare product in the first person. The same account had faked Olympic champions Deng Yaping and Guo Jingjing. WeChat Channels banned it permanently.
stories.twist: Reporters found sellers offering custom deepfake celebrity sales videos for about ¥1,000 a minute from one photo. About five weeks later (26 Nov) the brand behind the product apologised, removed the content and promised full refunds on the related orders; Wu's studio accepted (Sina Finance report, not yet confirmed by a second outlet).
stories.why: Imagine finding a video of yourself selling something you've never touched, in your own voice.
stories.result: Account banned (Yicai, GMW). Refunds on all related orders (Sina Finance, 26 Nov; amounts unknown). Sales before the ban: unknown.
stories.dates: Call-out 18 Oct 2026 · CCTV interview 20 Oct · brand apology ~26 Nov 2026

proof.label: Sina Finance (26 Nov, apology and refunds)
